sections.title: 2. Internal Components
sections.intro: **Each of these can be removed separately, which is useful for your repair and reuse argument:**

rows: Hard drive (2.5"), optical drive (CD/DVD), ExpressCard / hard-drive bay assembly
System board (motherboard), processor module, 2 memory modules, modem, Mini-Card (Wi-Fi), Bluetooth card, discrete video card (optional)
Processor thermal-cooling assembly, video-card cooling assembly, system fan
Display assembly: LCD panel, CCFL backlight lamp, inverter, LVDS video cable
Keyboard, palm rest with touchpad, hinge cover, speakers
Main battery, CR-2032 coin-cell battery, battery latch assembly
Sigmatel STAC9200 audio, Ricoh R5C832 card reader, 10/100 Ethernet

sections.title: 3. Carbon Footprint
sections.intro: A **carbon footprint** is the total amount of greenhouse gases (primarily carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide) generated directly and indirectly by an individual, organization, event, or product.

rows: Hybrid life-cycle study of laptops of this era (Deng, 2010)
63–71% of total energy for making and using
25 W average × 4 h/day = 36.5 kWh/year × India grid factor 0.716 kg CO₂/kWh (CEA)

sections.note: **Key insight:** most of this laptop's carbon was emitted in the factory, before it was ever switched on. Every extra year of reuse avoids building a new laptop, which is the strongest argument for Repair and Reuse before Recycle.

sections.title: 4. Metals and Materials Inside
sections.intro: Average amounts per laptop from published studies of laptop.

rows: Magnets: hard-drive head motor 725 mg, hard-drive spindle 319 mg, optical drive 464 mg, speakers 646 mg
Motherboard 56 mg, display board 18 mg, memory 15 mg, smaller boards about 5 mg each
Transparent conductive (ITO) layer of the LCD
Only in LED backlights (about 1.6 mg); a CCFL laptop like the 6400 has none

columns: How to dispose of it safely
rows: CCFL backlight lamp in the display
Toxic vapour; a few milligrams per lamp
Remove the CCFL lamp whole without breaking it, seal it in a glass jar, and hand it to an authorised e-waste recycler. If broken, ventilate, scoop debris, never vacuum.
Solder on circuit boards; units built before 1 July 2006 may contain leaded solder
Damages the nervous system; pollutes soil and water
Never desolder, burn or acid-wash the circuit boards. Send them whole to an authorised e-waste recycler, who safely recovers the lead along with gold, silver and copper.
6-cell or 9-cell main battery, plus CR-2032 coin cell
Fire risk if punctured or short-circuited; cobalt is toxic
Never put it in the dustbin. Tape the terminals, bag each battery separately, and give it to a battery recycler. Swollen batteries must not be charged, pressed or punctured.
Plastic casing, circuit boards, cable insulation
Never burn the plastic casing or cables to recover copper, as this releases toxic fumes. Hand all plastics and cables to an authorised e-waste recycler for controlled processing.
2 × DDR2 slots (tested unit: PC5300), up to 2 GB
Removable processor module; Dell supported Celeron M up to Core 2 Duo
2.5" SATA hard drive (tested unit: Hitachi HTS541060G9SA00), so a SATA SSD upgrade is possible
Lightweight Linux, offline lab or teaching PC, or donor for spare parts (RAM, optical drive, charger, keyboard)
The hard drive may still hold personal files, photos and passwords
**Clear** the drive: overwrite all user data (NIST SP 800-88)
**Purge** or **Destroy** the drive so data cannot be recovered even in a laboratory (NIST SP 800-88)
1. Main battery and coin cell → 2. CCFL lamp, removed whole → 3. Circuit boards, for precious-metal recovery → 4. Hard-drive magnets, for rare earths → 5. Plastics and metals
Under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), the producer must ensure its e-waste reaches authorised recyclers
Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 (India): landfilling and incineration of waste batteries are banned; all must be recycled or refurbished
Limits applied from 1 July 2006: lead, mercury, hexavalent chromium, PBB and PBDE 0.1%; cadmium 0.01%
Tin (solder), tantalum (about 1.7 g, capacitors) and gold (about 100–140 mg) – three of the four "3TG" conflict minerals
EU Regulation 2017/821 requires importers of 3TG minerals to carry out supply-chain due diligence. No such rule existed when this laptop was made in 2006
Recovered tin, tantalum and gold reduce the need for newly mined conflict minerals

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.subtitle: Conclusion for your project

rows: Recovers metals; doesn't avoid manufacturing a new laptop

sections.note: Reuse earns roughly 3–10 times more than scrap and saves far more carbon. This supports the Repair → Reuse → Recycle order your website recommends.
